citation.title: Multiscale characterization of commercial and landfill-recovered plastics in Songkhla province, Thailand

householdWasteClaim.quote: The city produces approximately 237.75 tons of household waste per day.
householdWasteClaim.quoteLocation: Section 2.1 'Site specification' (efetch XML body); the same sentence is present in the article HTML: yes
householdWasteClaim.kind: household waste generation as worded ('The city produces approximately 237.75 tons of household waste per day') — 'generated', not 'collected'
householdWasteClaim.citedSource: Hat Yai Municipality , Annual Waste Management Report 2024 , 2024 , [in Thai]
householdWasteClaim.referencePeriodNote: Not stated. The article (published 2025-07-11) gives no reference date/period for the figure; it cites a municipal report titled 'Annual Waste Management Report 2024' (in Thai), so the figure presumably refers to 2024 or FY2567, but the article does not say so.
householdWasteClaim.scope: Hat Yai Municipality ('the city' in the site description of Hat Yai Municipality, 21.00 km²), household waste only; whether commercial/tourism waste is included is not stated.
householdWasteClaim.methodologyNote: Not stated: no weighing, sampling or per-capita factor is described for this number. It is background information in the site description, not a result of the study (which characterises commercial PE/PP/PET/PVC and PE recovered from a local landfill in Songkhla province).
householdWasteClaim.assessment: Secondary citation only: verified that the article states 237.75 t/day and attributes it to 'Hat Yai Municipality, Annual Waste Management Report 2024 [in Thai]' (reference 32), which we could not locate online. Use as an 'estimated' (cited) generation figure with this caveat, never as 'observed'.

context.note: For comparison only. The LAO survey (Songkhla catalog dataset_10_27) reports 101002.212 t/year generated in FY2565 (2021-10-01..2022-09-30) = 276.72 t/day (derived); definitions and years differ, so the two figures are not interchangeable.

populationClaim.quote: Covering an area of 21.00 km 2 , Hat Yai Municipality had an estimated population of approximately 191 696 in 2024, making it the fourth-largest city municipality in Thailand.
populationClaim.citedSource: Department of Provincial Administration , Statistical Yearbook Thailand 2024 , Ministry of Interior , Thailand , 2024

composition.quote: 32 The major components of the municipal waste stream are consistent with those observed in other urban centers in Southeast Asia: organic waste—including food scraps and garden residues—accounts for the largest proportion, followed by plastic waste from commercial and household sources (such as packaging materials and single-use plastics), as well as glass and metal containers.
composition.citedSource: United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) , Regional Waste Management Outlook for Asia and the Pacific , 2023
composition.assessment: No composition table for Hat Yai exists in the article; tables present: Mechanical properties of selected plastics a | FTIR analysis: (a) PE, (b) PP, (c) PET, (d) PVC, (e) PE (LF).. The text only ranks components qualitatively (organic largest, then plastic, then glass and metal) citing a regional UNEP outlook. No percentage shares can be mapped to organic/plastic/paper/glassMetal/hazardous/other.
